subject: Recap: Renewal strategy + RAG/burst workload proposal and timeline
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Chen <alex@luminix.ai>, Chris Green <chris.green@luminix.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Renewal strategy + RAG/burst workload proposal and timeline

Hi Alex / Chris —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap so we’re aligned and can move toward the December renewal with a clear expansion path: 

Key pain points you reiterated
- Current latency spikes during nightly batch RAG jobs are causing timeouts in search pipelines.
- Token cost for h2 inference (long-context summarization) up ~3x month-over-month due to duplicate work and lack of prefix caching.
- Compliance requirement: audit logs for inference requests must be retained for 90 days in your EU region for regs we spoke about.

Goals we agreed on
1) Stabilize p95 latency under 350ms for 512-token calls for production search by Nov.
2) Reduce per-token bill for RAG and long-context pipelines by at least 30% through caching + quantized model variants.
3) Pilot Dedicated capacity for burst RAG jobs (weekend heavy runs) ahead of renewal to validate unit economics.

Proposed next steps (timeline)
- Week of Sep 20: Redwood provides a 2-week dedicated pilot run proposal (capacity, pricing, success metrics). Action: Markus to send proposal (attached).
- Oct 4–15: Pilot run window (we’ll reserve a dedicated pool with burst policy).
- Oct 20: Post-pilot review (usage report + latency report) and pricing adjustment discussion.
- Nov 10: Finalize renewal amendment and capacity commit for Dec 1 start.

What we’ll deliver in the pilot
- Reserved Dedicated pool for specified instance types, autoscale to handle weekend burst.
- Prefix/KV caching enabled for your RAG pipeline and config suggestions to reduce duplicate tokens.
- Quantized model variant suggestion (4-bit) for embed+inference where appropriate.
- 90-day audit logging option (EU region) with sample retention export.

Please see attached the proposal and the usage snapshot we pulled from your account (Aug 2026). If that aligns, can we lock a pilot start date the week of Oct 4? If you’d like, I can book a short 30-min kickoff next week to walk the team through the pilot configs.

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: Luminix_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal, pricing tiers) | usage_report_aug2026.csv (summary of token usage by workload)

From: Alex Chen <alex@luminix.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Cc: Chris Green <chris.green@luminix.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Renewal strategy + RAG/burst workload proposal and timeline

Markus —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side before we confirm the Oct pilot window: 
- For the Dedicated pool, what GPU families are you proposing (A100 vs H100 equivalents)? We run heavy multi-document RAG and want to ensure memory headroom.
- Can the audit logs be limited to specific teams/projects (we don’t need system-level debug logs retained)?
- On the 30% cost reduction target: is that achievable purely via caching + quantized variants, or would you expect model changes as well?

If those answers look reasonable, we’re inclined to greenlight the Oct 4 pilot. Booking a 30-min kickoff next Tue/Thu would be great.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of ML Platform, Luminix AI
alex@luminix.ai

On Sat, Sep 12, 2026 at 3:05 PM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference> wrote:
> [original message]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Chen <alex@luminix.ai>, Chris Green <chris.green@luminix.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Renewal strategy + RAG/burst workload proposal and timeline

Alex —

Short answers: 
- GPU families: We recommend an H100-equivalent profile for the weekend RAG burst (memory + throughput), with an A100-equivalent fallback for non-burst steady state. The pilot proposal includes both options so you can validate memory headroom.
- Audit logs: Yes — retention can be scoped to selected projects and request types. We’ll provide an export schema so your compliance team can validate before the pilot.
- 30% target: Achievable in many cases via prefix/KV caching + quantization and smarter batching. We’ll include model-variant impact estimates in the pilot proposal (it’s part of the attached PDF). In case we need extra savings, model-selection recommendations are an incremental lever.

I’ll send a short calendar invite for a 30-min kickoff on Thu Sep 23 at 10:00am PT — does that work for you and Chris? If not, propose an alternate slot.

Also looping Monica (CS lead) and Vanessa (Solutions) to prep the pilot checklist and the internal engineering runbook.

Thanks,

Markus

On Mon, Sep 14, 2026 at 08:12 AM Alex Chen <alex@luminix.ai> wrote:

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: pricing options for Luminix pilot (need input before kickoff)

Monica / Vanessa —

Following the Luminix thread above: they’re comfortable moving to an Oct 4 pilot pending confirmation on GPU families and scoped audit logs. I attached the proposal I sent them. Need your input on two things before I lock the kickoff: 

1) Pricing breaks for H100 vs A100-equivalent pools for the 3-week pilot window (Oct 4–22). We need a conservative and an aggressive pricing scenario so we can propose both to Alex.
2) Success metrics: I suggest we track p95 latency (512 tokens), token cost per successful RAG call, and cache hit rate. Anything to add?

Can you send suggested numbers by EOD Wed Sep 15 so I can finalize the pilot doc and calendar invite? I’ll own the kickoff call.

Thanks — Markus
